A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeND/EES research. Their text, figures, equations, references, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia checkpoint analyses, dropout experiments, EES timing measurements, and HELM/MedHALT training results, including a FactScore comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Llama and LegalBench evaluations, hyperparameter studies, HaluEval results, and RAG comparisons.

M1.justification: The embedding extraction, variability calculation, deterministic top-K dropout, and EES computation retain the same algorithmic operations. v1 already defined Sensitive Neurons as embedding indices, so renaming them Sensitive Embedding Indices does not change the method. The RAG combination is an additional evaluation, without a revised SeND algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds LegalBench legal-reasoning data to the HELM/Wikipedia and MedHALT training evaluations. It also explicitly evaluates HaluEval QA and summarization scenarios, beyond v1's generic mention of HaluEval. Existing XSum coverage remains, with its plot moved to Appendix A.2.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds evaluated RAG and SeND-plus-RAG comparisons; v1 only discussed RAG as complementary. Ordinary training, inference-time random dropout, and the EigenScore timing comparator remain. v1's caption-only finding that ordinary training outperformed random dropout is omitted.

E3.justification: v2 adds Llama 3.2 1B and Llama 3.1 8B configurations, HaluEval metrics, perplexity, and a 1,000-point FactScore evaluation alongside the retained 100-point test. Section 4.1 now specifies 200 training examples across datasets and 2,000 for MedHALT, whereas v1 stated both sizes for both original datasets. The three-epoch window is redescribed as three checkpoints; this does not establish that original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests dropout rates of 10%, 20%, and 30% across three domains and step thresholds of 1, 2, 3, and 4 on LegalBench. These studies examine parameter sensitivity and support the selected defaults, replacing v1's computation-based justification for choosing three epochs. Earlier dropout diagnostics and EES moment analyses remain.

E5.justification: The original five-run shaded training plots reappear as Figure 15, now explicitly identified as showing standard deviations. Figure 11 additionally specifies ten-run averaging for the LegalBench dropout-rate ablation. This expands statistical documentation without establishing additional runs for the original results; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial model, domain, metric, and ablation results. Table 1 retains the 100-point FactScores of 0.07/0.05 and adds 1,000-point scores of 0.08/0.06 for SeND/normal training. New HaluEval results are accuracy 0.016/0.014, correctness 0.027/0.027, and exact match 0.589/0.496. Section 4.2 reports RAG at 0.25 and SeND plus RAG at 0.28, but its standalone SeND score of 0.07 on 1,000 points conflicts with Table 1.

T1.justification: Definitions 3.1–3.4, Lemma 1, Proposition 1, and the EES derivation in Appendix B retain the same mathematics. Renaming neurons as embedding indices and explaining the activation-matrix symbol do not introduce new definitions, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and headline claims of up to 40% FactScore improvement and approximately twofold EES speedup remain. v2 broadens the stated demonstrated scope to LegalBench and Llama, explicitly claims applicability to all training stages in the conclusion, and adds the categorical claim that SeND is the first method focused on hallucinations during LLM training.

C2.justification: v1's explanation that weak MedHALT gains may reflect previously unseen data, potentially requiring delayed dropout, is removed. v2 introduces a tentative generalization-based explanation for stronger LegalBench benefits, discusses mixed medical-domain behavior, and explicitly acknowledges that only finetuning was tested. It also removes the contradictory statement that reducing EigenScore increases uncertainty.

D1.justification: v2 documents tested hyperparameter ranges and their selection, including Appendix C's 30% dropout exception for Llama 3.1 8B. That exception conflicts with the main text and Figure 4's blanket 20% setting, leaving the exact configuration unclear. The generation temperature, embedding extraction details, and code/data access link were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Guha et al. on LegalBench and Lewis et al. on RAG, and removes Black et al. on GPT-NeoX. It strengthens novelty positioning with an explicit first-training-focused-method claim and adds empirical discussion of complementarity with RAG. The broader related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from Sensitive Neuron Dropout to Sensitivity Dropout and Sensitive Embedding Indices. v2 condenses introductory material, moves metric discussion from related work into motivation, merges the separate Section 2 methods subsection into its opening, and revises the experimental narrative. The principal section sequence and most technical exposition remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and multiple metric, ablation, and Llama training figures. Figure 4 becomes a four-panel model/domain comparison. The original XSum panel moves to Figure 7, and the original shaded Pythia training plots move to Figure 15; training curves are also redisplayed without shading. These substantially change the visual presentation while retaining earlier evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the evaluation more informative through Llama and LegalBench tests, parameter ablations, expanded factuality evaluation, and an actual RAG-combination comparison. These strengthen support beyond v1's limited SeND validation. The net gain is constrained by conflicting 1,000-point FactScores and Llama dropout settings, plus Figure 14's claim of consistent superiority despite its MedHALT panel ending with worse EES for SeND.
